    Introduction

    a1_Introduction.Rmd

    scCNVis is an R package for exploring single-cell copy number data. All plotting functions take as input an scCNVis object. Example data has been provided to show how this is done.

    First, is the example input matrix containing the copy number values:

    library(scCNVis)

#Example matrix
#Rows = cells, Columns = Genomc regions, Values = Copy number values (or a similar metric)
#Row names and column names are optional, because the cell names and column
#info will be provided separately
matrix <- example.matrix
print(dim(matrix))
#> [1] 1000 2813
print(matrix[1:5,1:5])
#>           [,1]      [,2]      [,3]      [,4]      [,5]
#> [1,] 0.5428811 0.5462523 0.5754694 0.4448817 0.4349184
#> [2,] 0.7396058 0.7228345 0.7058930 0.5595001 0.5302412
#> [3,] 0.9302811 0.9243288 0.9962392 1.0133404 1.0446618
#> [4,] 0.7797723 0.7950255 0.7920179 0.7929032 0.7816027
#> [5,] 0.8720612 0.8505887 0.8709961 0.8086944 0.8133054

    Second, is the example cell names:

    
cells <- example.cells
#The number of cell names should be the same as the number of rows as the input
#matrix, and should be in the same order as those rows
print(length(cells))
#> [1] 1000
print(cells[1:5])
#> [1] "cell-1" "cell-2" "cell-3" "cell-4" "cell-5"

    Third, is a GenomicRanges::GRanges object. It should have the same length as the number of columns in the input matrix, where each entry describes a genomic bin. Bins are expected to be region-sorted and non-overlapping.

    granges <- example.granges
print(granges)
#> GRanges object with 2813 ranges and 0 metadata columns:
#>          seqnames            ranges strand
#>             <Rle>         <IRanges>  <Rle>
#>      [1]     chr1   1000000-2000000      *
#>      [2]     chr1   2000000-3000000      *
#>      [3]     chr1   3000000-4000000      *
#>      [4]     chr1   4000000-5000000      *
#>      [5]     chr1   5000000-6000000      *
#>      ...      ...               ...    ...
#>   [2809]     chrY 15000000-16000000      *
#>   [2810]     chrY 16000000-17000000      *
#>   [2811]     chrY 19000000-20000000      *
#>   [2812]     chrY 20000000-21000000      *
#>   [2813]     chrY 21000000-22000000      *
#>   -------
#>   seqinfo: 24 sequences from an unspecified genome; no seqlengths

    Finally, is the input meta data. This is a data.frame where each row corresponds to a cell. At a minimum, this should have a Sample column describing what sample the cell came from, but can include an arbitrary amount of other data as well. Row names should be the provided cell names.

    meta <- example.meta
print(dim(meta))
#> [1] 1000    1
print(head(meta))
#>         Sample
#> cell-1 SampleA
#> cell-2 SampleA
#> cell-3 SampleA
#> cell-4 SampleA
#> cell-5 SampleA
#> cell-6 SampleA

    These inputs can be used to create a scCNVis object.

    obj <- scCNVis::createPlotObject(input.matrix = matrix,
                                 cell.names = cells,
                                 granges = granges,
                                 meta = meta)

    Documentation about making frequency plots, heatmaps and lineplots show how to use this object to generate plots.
